{"id": "4:36/q39", "question": "What is the overall scope and authority of this command to kindness?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:36/q39/p1", "position": "It binds people to care for every listed group, with fitting forms of kindness for each.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī stresses care and compassion for all and fidelity to God's and the Messenger's directions. Ālūsī says the required degree differs by recipient; Kur'an Yolu includes neighbors, companions, travelers and dependents, and Study Quran emphasizes those with less social power. Ṭabrisī calls the verse a gathering of Islam's pillars and good character; Ṭabāṭabāʾ says many reports of concrete kindness are too numerous to reproduce."}, {"id": "4:36/q39/p2", "position": "Its ethical rule is definitive, agreed, and unabrogated.", "reasons": "Qurṭubī says all scriptures give similar commands and reason alone recognizes their force; Study Quran transmits his observation."}, {"id": "4:36/q39/p3", "position": "Earlier treatment of kin, orphans, and the poor is cross-referenced to al-Baqara.", "reasons": "Qurṭubī points readers to that earlier discussion."}]}
{"id": "4:36/q40", "question": "What does Jishumī's surrounding discussion say about Ali's arbitration?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:36/q40/p1", "position": "It was justified by danger and division in his army, and compared with other peace decisions.", "reasons": "Jishumī reports his teachers' defense of Ali against the Kharijites: after Qur'ans were raised his army split and he feared for his life, so arbitration was permissible or obligatory. He compares the Prophet's Hudaybiyya agreement and Hasan's peace after attack, Ubayd Allah b. Abbas seeking safety, and military fracture. He invokes God's guidance of those intending good."}]}
{"id": "4:36/q41", "question": "What recitation practices are discussed in the materials attached to this verse?", "turns_on": "Purity level and pedagogical or memory exceptions.", "positions": [{"id": "4:36/q41/p1", "position": "Recitation in minor impurity is allowed, though ablution is recommended; major impurity and menstruation receive stricter limits.", "reasons": "Burhān and Itqān report al-Juwaynī allowing recitation without ablution and the Prophet's practice. Itqān recommends ablution, pauses during passing wind, and notes prohibition on voiced recitation during major impurity or menstruation with looking or inward recitation still possible. {"id": "4:36/q42", "question": "How does believers' unity inform kindness?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:36/q42/p1", "position": "People of truth are one soul despite distinct bodies and numbers.", "reasons": "Bursawī grounds their solidarity in undiminished unity of faith."}]}
{"id": "4:42/q01", "question": "What day does يَوْمَئِذٍ indicate?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q01/p1", "position": "The Day of Resurrection when prophetic witnesses are brought.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī and Study Quran connect it to 4:41, when a witness is brought from each community and Muḥammad over his community; al-Wāḥidī, al-Baghawī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya locate the wish on that very day."}]}
{"id": "4:42/q02", "question": "What governs يَوْمَئِذٍ grammatically?", "turns_on": "Whether the time phrase attaches to the wish or to the preceding witness clause.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q02/p1", "position": "It is an adverb governed by يَوَدُّ.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās also allows yawm to be indeclinable; al-Ṭabrisī and Abū Ḥayyān say it modifies the wish. {"id": "4:42/q03", "question": "How is the form يَوْمَئِذٍ constructed?", "turns_on": "The grammatical treatment of yawm and idh, and which omitted earlier clause the tanwīn replaces.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q03/p1", "position": "Yawm is annexed to idh, and idh's tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī says idh normally takes a nominal or verbal clause and cites 40:71, 2:30, 2:72, 70:11 and 30:43; al-Quṭāmī's poetry illustrates a nominal clause. Abū Ḥayyān and al-Samīn allow either both prior witness clauses, the first, or the last; those choices affect whether الرسول is generic or Muḥammad. Al-Ṭabrisī calls the tanwīn a mark of completion."}, {"id": "4:42/q03/p2", "position": "Yawm can be built as indeclinable by annexation to indeclinable idh.", "reasons": "Al-Ḥawfī gives the rule that an adverb annexed to an indeclinable may be built; Abū Ḥayyān approves, reasoning that annexation specifies idh like a noun. {"id": "4:42/q04", "question": "What does يَوَدُّ mean here?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q04/p1", "position": "It means to wish or desire.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān glosses it with yatamannā; al-Wāḥidī refers to his earlier discussion at 2:96."}]}
{"id": "4:42/q05", "question": "Who are ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟?", "turns_on": "Whether the description is read as its outward referent or an inward state.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q05/p1", "position": "The disbelievers, especially those who denied God or His oneness.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī says they deny God's oneness; Muslim al-Baṭīn identifies those wishing for leveling as disbelievers. {"id": "4:42/q06", "question": "How are كَفَرُوا۟ and عَصَوُا۟ related?", "turns_on": "Whether the conjunction joins verbs of one relative clause, an elided second relative, or a circumstantial clause.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q06/p1", "position": "The two verbs describe one group who both disbelieved and disobeyed.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī says conjunction implies distinct sins; Abū Ḥayyān calls this the apparent syntax. {"id": "4:42/q07", "question": "What does their disobedience to the Messenger mean?", "turns_on": "Whether عصوا is read as additional legal sins, the Prophet's governing commands, or inward failure to follow him.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q07/p1", "position": "It comprises acts of disobedience beyond disbelief.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī argues that otherwise the conjunction is redundant and infers that disbelievers face Islam's practical obligations and added punishment; al-Ālūsī likewise infers accountability for derivative duties. {"id": "4:42/q08", "question": "Who does ٱلرَّسُولَ designate?", "turns_on": "Which earlier witness clause supplies the context, and whether the singular title is generic.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q08/p1", "position": "Muhammad specifically.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī names Muhammad as witness over his community; al-Samīn says a tanwīn replacing only the preceding وجئنا بك makes this specific. {"id": "4:42/q10", "question": "How is the wāw in عَصَوُا۟ pronounced?", "turns_on": "Which vowel resolves adjacent sukūns and whether the original kasra is retained.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q10/p1", "position": "With ḍamma.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj prefers it to resolve two adjacent sukūns; al-Naḥḥās and al-Qurṭubī also allow kasra. {"id": "4:42/q11", "question": "How is تُسَوَّىٰ read?", "turns_on": "Passive leveling versus reflexive leveling, and whether the reflexive tāʾ assimilates or is omitted; al-Ṭabarī also weighs ease of pronunciation and 78:40.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q11/p1", "position": "With ḍamma on tāʾ and a light sīn: a passive verb, 'the earth is made level.'", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr and others are named, although source lists vary; the agent is unexpressed and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān identify God as agent. Al-Ṭabarī notes all three readings have the dust sense. Qirāʾāt ER calls this earth's passive leveling."}, {"id": "4:42/q11/p2", "position": "With fatḥa on tāʾ and doubled sīn: assimilated reflexive تتسوى.", "reasons": "Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir are regularly named, with Medinan and Syrian readers or Abū Jaʿfar/Yazīd in some lists. The tāʾ assimilates into sīn, giving the earth active/reflexive agency; al-Rāzī compares 27:47, 10:24 and 6:26. Ibn al-Jawzī reports Abū ʿAlī's explanation that the people become level with earth."}, {"id": "4:42/q11/p3", "position": "With fatḥa on tāʾ and light sīn: a tāʾ is omitted from تتسوى.", "reasons": "Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī are commonly named, Khalaf by Ibn al-Jazarī and Ibn ʿĀshūr; some report Kufans except ʿĀṣim. Al-Ṭabarī prefers this lighter reading, avoiding two doubled consonants and fitting 78:40; imāla is praised by Abū ʿAlī and reported by later sources. Al-Thaʿlabī compares 11:105."}]}
{"id": "4:42/q12", "question": "How may the pronoun in بِهِمُ be pronounced?", "turns_on": "Dialectal pronoun vowels, adjacency to bāʾ, and the liaison vowel at the word boundary.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q12/p1", "position": "With ḍamma on both hāʾ and mīm.", "reasons": "Ibn Khālawayh says this restores their original vowels before bāʾ; al-Zajjāj allows ḍamma on mīm. Qirāʾāt ER identifies ḍamma on hāʾ in bihumu with Hijazi and Tamimi dialects."}, {"id": "4:42/q12/p2", "position": "With kasra on both hāʾ and mīm.", "reasons": "Ibn Khālawayh attributes the vowels to adjacency to bāʾ and the following word boundary; Qirāʾāt ER calls mīm's kasra a liaison vowel before a pause or consonant."}, {"id": "4:42/q12/p3", "position": "With kasra on hāʾ but original mīm vowel.", "reasons": "Ibn Khālawayh says the hāʾ follows neighboring bāʾ, and the following wāw drops for ease."}]}
{"id": "4:42/q13", "question": "How does لَوْ function after يَوَدُّ?", "turns_on": "Whether لو is a nominalizing particle like أن or a conditional with understood object and answer.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q13/p1", "position": "It nominalizes its clause, which is the object of يَوَدُّ.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān compares أن and says there is no conditional answer. {"id": "4:42/q16", "question": "What do they wish would happen with the earth?", "turns_on": "Whether leveling means burial, conversion to dust, nonresurrection, animal-like dust, trampling, ransom, or an inward erasure; the readings and بِ are used to support some views.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q16/p1", "position": "The earth would split or rise, swallow them, and close level over them.", "reasons": "Muqātil, Mujāz, Qatāda, Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Jurayj give variants of entering, being swallowed or covered; Ibn ʿAbbās adds mountains flattened over them. Ibn Kathīr cites the terrors and 78:40; al-Qurṭubī situates the wish after limbs expose them."}, {"id": "4:42/q16/p2", "position": "They would themselves become dust or one substance with earth.", "reasons": "Al-Farrāʾ, Ibn Qutayba, al-Ṭabarī, Ibn ʿAbbās and many later sources present this sense; 78:40 is repeatedly cited. {"id": "4:42/q19", "question": "Why can they conceal nothing from God?", "turns_on": "Whether exposure comes through bodily testimony, divine knowledge, Hell's keepers, confession, or the inward disclosure of the soul.", "positions": [{"id": "4:42/q19/p1", "position": "Their limbs testify after their mouths are sealed, exposing them.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās repeatedly tells how denial of shirk fails when hands, feet or other body parts speak, citing 6:23 and 36:65.
